name: JWA's And Justice For All

date.source: The fed's own served broadcast title: "JWA's Blind Justice: 9.5.99" style dating on its own sister PPVs; this show's own opening line bills it "the first JWA sponsored PPV."

appearances.note: Billed to present the JWA Hardcore Title to its winner; the match itself is not in the served part.
Billed against Faith for the vacant Hardcore Title; the match itself is not in the served part.
Billed against Mass Carnage for the vacant Hardcore Title; the match itself is not in the served part.
Billed defending the TV Title against Gangrene; the match itself is not in the served part.
Billed challenging Oasis for the TV Title; the match itself is not in the served part.

notes: The promotion's own debut PPV, staged as a twenty-man battle royal narrowing the field toward ladder matches for the vacant World, Trans-Atlantic, and Hardcore Titles. This served part covers the battle royal's own opening eliminations: Wildwing clears the ring of four opponents in short order before Polar Bear ambushes him with a chair. The remaining five parts (not served) carry the show through to its own title-match finishes.

eliminations.note: Kicked from the apron to the guardrail with a Sweet Dreams kick, after being tossed there.
Sidestepped by Wildwing into the entering Sugar Ray, sending both men over the top in the same spot.
Same spot as Lucky Rich, seconds into his own entrance.

matches.note: The served part (1 of 6) cuts off mid-match, immediately after Bounty Hunter's entrance ("Click Here for More Action"); no winner is shown in the held text — the World Title's own eventual result is attested only by "Blind Justice"'s own recap (see jwa-ajfa-world-r001).

name: JWA's Dark Justice

date.source: The fed's own served broadcast title: "JWA's Dark Justice: 11.14.99."

notes: The held record's latest dated show. This served part opens on Jose Gonzalez defending (and losing) the TV Title against Chad Hazzard, then closes on the World Title main event: Bryan Mercy defends against War, with the M.o.A stable (Fury, Faith, Attict, Jose) running in to turn the tide before a returning masked referee, "Smokey," counts Mercy's pinfall. Sweet Lou: "Your winner and still World Champion Bryan Mercy!!!" An out-of-character sign-off credits four names (Teck, JT, Andrew L., Matt L.) for writing help — handles and initials, standing per the privacy rule's own bare-first-name-and-initials exception. Malibu Magee (billed "back in the JWA") separately knocks Chad Hazzard out backstage with a frozen salami after the TV Title match, unconnected to the M.o.A. beatdown.

matches.note: Jose Gonzalez, escorted by fellow M.o.A. members Chris Fury, Matt Attict and Redemption, fails to take the title back from champion Chad Hazzard (accompanied by manager Lana Jones). The M.o.A. beats Hazzard down after the bell — Fury with a chair, Attict with the title belt, Redemption holding him up for Fury's "Frustration."

Champion Matt Attict retains against Preacher with interference from Jose Gonzalez and Chris Fury (a trip, a beatdown while the referee is distracted). Post-match, the masked "Mysterio" runs in and diamond-cuts Attict — revealed moments later, in a separate promo, to be Savage Warrior.

Champion Bryan Mercy retains the main event against War. The M.o.A. (Jose Gonzalez, Chris Fury, Faith, Matt Attict) run in mid-match; the returning masked referee "Smokey" zip-lines in from the upper deck and repels them (exchanging blows with commentator Tommy Riley along the way) before revealing himself and counting Mercy's pinfall.

name: JWA's Blind Justice

date.source: Cited by the World Title reign ledger (jwa-ajfa-world-r002), quoting the fed's own recap: "Mercy jumps and he makes it to the platform he has the belts."

evidence.note: The fed's own site holds three parts of "Blind Justice" at geocities.com/jwrestling/PPV/ (per the closure-candidates vault mirror); none is served in the held record.

Both reigns cite this show's own recap package for the World Title's founding-reign confirmation, the Jon Clark intervening reign, and Bryan Mercy's own Triple Threat Ladder Match win — all read from the recap quoted in those rows, not from a served Blind Justice document.

notes: The held record's middle PPV, between "And Justice For All" (22 August 1999) and "Dark Justice" (14 November 1999). Its own recap package is the sole surviving source for the World Title changing from Keith Wildwing to Jon Clark to Bryan Mercy — none of it captured as a served document.
